title: Copy a project to a new computer

story.speaker: Sam
story.text: I am on the lab computer today. There is no festival folder here at all.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Then **clone** it. Cloning downloads the whole project, with all its history.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: You are on the lab computer now. Look at the prompt: it says `lab`, not `laptop`.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Clone into your home folder. Git makes the folder for you and names it after the project.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Clone also sets up `origin` for you. You never type `git remote add` after a clone.

items.text: Clone the festival site onto the lab computer
The clone has the project history

hints: There is nothing here to work with yet. You need to download the project first.
`git clone <address>` downloads a whole project and its history into a new folder.
recap: `git clone <address>` downloads a project with its full history and sets up `origin` for you.

cheatSheet.summary: Download a whole project with its history

predict.question: How much of the project history does a clone download?

choices.text: Only the newest version of each file

predict.explanation: A clone is a full copy. You get every commit, so you can read the whole history offline.
